questions.q:
The equilibrium constant for the reaction
$\mathrm{SO}_2(g)+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{SO}_3(g)$ is $5 \times 10^{-2}$ atm.
The equilibrium constant of the reaction
$2 \mathrm{SO}_3(g) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{SO}_2(g)+\mathrm{O}_2(g)$ would be
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{SO}_2+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2 & \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{SO}_3 \\ K_1 & =\frac{\left[\mathrm{SO}_3\right]}{\left[\mathrm{SO}_2\right]\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]^{1 / 2}} \\ 2 \mathrm{SO}_3 & \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{SO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2 \\ \mathrm{~K}_2 & =\frac{\left[\mathrm{SO}_2\right]^2\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]}{\left[\mathrm{SO}_3\right]^2}\end{aligned}$
From Eqs. (i) and (ii)
$\begin{aligned} K_2 & =\frac{1}{K_1^2} \\ K_2 & =\frac{1}{\left(5 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2}=\frac{1}{25 \times 10^{-4}} \\ & =\frac{100 \times 10^2}{25} \\ & =4 \times 10^2 \mathrm{~atm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Consider the following reaction in a $1 \mathrm{~L}$ closed vessel. \mathrm{N}_2+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NH}_3 If all the species; $\mathrm{N}_2, \mathrm{H}_2$ and $\mathrm{NH}_3$ are in $1 \mathrm{~mol}$ in the beginning of the reaction and equilibrium is attained after unreacted $\mathrm{N}_2$ is $0.7 \mathrm{~mol}$. What is the value of equilibrium constant?
questions.solution: For the given reaction: $\mathrm{N}}_{2}+3 \mathrm{H}}_{2} $\rightleftharpoons$2 $\mathrm{NH}}_{3} \begin{array}{llll}\text { Initial moles }$ \text{ and }  1  \text{ and }  1  \text{ and }  1\end{array} At equilibrium $1-x \quad 1-3 x \quad 2 x$ Given, $1-x=0.7 $\mathrm{~mol}\therefore \quadx=$0.3 $\mathrm{~mol}Therefore, concentration of $\mathrm{N}}_{2}, \mathrm{H}}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{NH}}_{3}$ at equilibrium will be \begin{aligned} ${\left[\mathrm{N}_2\right] }$ \text{ and } =[0.7] \\ ${\left[\mathrm{H}_2\right] }$ \text{ and } =1-(3 $\times$0.3)=[0.1] \\ ${\left[\mathrm{NH}_3\right] }$ \text{ and } =1+2 x=1+(2 $\times$0.3)=[1.6] \end{aligned} According to law of equilibrium constant \left($K_C\right)\begin{aligned}$K_C \text{ and } $=\frac{\left[\mathrm{NH}_3\right]^2}{\left[\mathrm{~N}^2\right],\left[\mathrm{H}_2\right]^3}=\frac{[\mathrm{l} .6]^2}{[0.7][0.1]^3}$\\ K_C \text{ and } $=\frac{(256)}{0.007}=$3657.14 \end{aligned} Hence, equilibrium constant \left($K_C\right)=3657.14$ and (b) is the correct option.$

questions.q: For the reaction $A\left(g\right) ⇌ B\left(g\right) + C\left(g\right), A$ is $33 %$ dissociated at a total pressure $P .$~The correct relation between $P$ and ${K}_{p}$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

Total pressure$= P$

Degree of dissociation $= 33 % = 0 . 33$~

The given equilibrium reaction is,

$\begin{cases} & A ( g ) & ⇌ & B ( g ) & + & C ( g ) \\ att = 0 & 1 & & 0 & & 0 \\ att = {T}_{eq} & 1 - \alpha & & \alpha & & \alpha\end{cases}$

Now, Total number of moles~$= 1 - \alpha + \alpha + \alpha = 1 + \alpha$~

Partial pressure of~$A = \left(\dfrac{1 - \alpha}{1 + \alpha}\right) \times P$

Partial pressure of~$B = \left(\dfrac{α}{1 + \alpha}\right) \times P$

Partial pressure of~$C = \left(\dfrac{α}{1 + \alpha}\right) \times P$

The relation between the~${K}_{P}$~and the total pressure is,

${K}_{P} = \dfrac{{P}_{B} \times {P}_{C}}{PA}$

Putting all the values of partial pressure, we get

${K}_{P} = {α}^{2}P \left(1 - {α}^{2}\right)$

${K}_{P} = \left(0 . 33\right)2P \left[1 - \left(0 . 33\right)2\right]$

${K}_{P} = 0 . 122P$

$P = 8 . 19{K}_{P}$

$P \approx8{K}_{P}$

Thus, the relation between $P$ and~${K}_{P}$~is~$P = 8{K}_{P}$

questions.q: At $T(K), K_C$ value for the reaction $\frac{1}{3} \mathrm{~N}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons \frac{2}{3} \mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{~g})$ is 50 . The $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{C}}$ value for the reaction $2 \mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{~g})+3 \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g})$ at the same temperature is
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{3} \mathrm{~N}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons \frac{2}{3} \mathrm{NH}_3 \mathrm{~K}_{\mathrm{C}}=50$ given. Multiply by 3 in eq ${ }^{\text {n }}$ \therefore \quad $\mathrm{N}}_{2}+3 \mathrm{H}}_{2} $\rightleftharpoons$2 $\mathrm{NH}}_{3} \text {. }Reverse eq (2) \therefore \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{C}}^{\prime}=(50)^3 \begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad 2 \mathrm{NH}}_{3} $\rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}}_{2}+3 \mathrm{H}}_{2} $\mathrm{~K}_{\mathrmC^{\prime}}=\left(\frac{1}{50}\right)^3 \\ & \therefore \quad $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrmC^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{50} \times \frac{1}{50} \times \frac{1}{50}=$8 $\times$10^{-6} . \end{aligned}

questions.q: In which of the following plots, an endothermic reaction is correctly represented?
questions.solution: $K_p$ and $T$ are related as follows : $K_p=K_c \cdot(R T)^{\Delta z_g}$ where, $\begin{aligned} & K_p=\text { Equilibrium constant in pressure terms } \\ & K_c=\text { Equilibrium constant in concentration terms. } \\ & \begin{aligned} R & =\text { Gas constant } \\ T & =\text { Temperature } \\ \Delta n_g & =\text { Gaseous moles of products } \\ & \quad-\text { gaseous moles of reactants }\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$ Therefore, $K_p \propto T \quad$ (for another reaction) Thus, the plot between $\frac{1}{T}$ and $\ln K_F$ shows a downward straight line slope for $\ln K_p$. Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.solution: For the reaction, \(\begin{aligned} \mathrm{CO}}_{2}(g)+ \mathrm{C}(s) \text{ and } \rightleftharpoons2 \mathrm{CO}(g) \\ K_{\mathrm{sp}}= \text{ and } $\frac{\left[\mathrm{CO}^2(g)\right.}{\left[\mathrm{CO}_2\right](g)}=\frac{p\left[\mathrm{CO}^2(g)\right.}{p\left[\mathrm{CO}_2\right](g)}$\\ \text{ and } {\left[\thereforep V=n R T \text { or } $\frac{n}{V}=\frac{p}{R T}, \frac{n}{V} \proptop($R, T)\right] } \end{aligned}\) Given, \$(\begin{aligned}$p[\mathrm{CO}] \text{ and } =0.6 \text { bar }\\ p\left[\mathrm{CO}}_{2}\right] \text{ and } =0.15 $\text { bar }$\\ K_p \text{ and } =\frac{[0.6]^2}{[0.15]}=2.4 \end{aligned}\) Also, \(K_p=K_c $\cdot($R T)^{\Delta$n}\) where, \($\Delta$n=\) moles of gaseous products moles of gaseous reactants \(=2-1=1\) \(\therefore \quad K_p=K_c $\times$R $\times$T\) where, \$(\begin{aligned}$K_c \text{ and } =$\frac{K_p}{R T}$\\ K_p \text{ and } =2.4 \\ R \text{ and } =0.082 $\mathrm{~L} \mathrm{~atm} \mathrm{~K} \end{aligned}$\) or \(K_c=2.89 $\times$10^{-2}\) Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.$

questions.q:
Ammonium sulphide and ammonium selenide on heating dissociates as

(NH4)2S(s) $⇌$ 2NH3(g)+ H2S(g); Kp1 = 9 × 10-3 atm3

(NH4)2Se(s) $⇌$ 2NH3(g) + H2Se(g); Kp2 = 4.5 × 10-3 atm3

The total pressure over the solid mixture at equilibrium is
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{ll}{\left({\text{NH}}_{4}\right)}_{2} \text{S}\left(\text{s}\right) ⇌ {\text{2NH}}_{3} \left(\text{g}\right) + {H}_{2} \text{S}\left(\text{g}\right) \\ \text{2p}\text{p}\end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll}{\left({\text{NH}}_{4}\right)}_{2} \text{Se}\left(\text{s}\right) ⇌ {\text{2NH}}_{3} \left(\text{g}\right) + {H}_{2} \text{Se}\left(\text{g}\right) \\ \text{2q}\text{q}\end{array}$

${K}_{\text{p} 1} = {\left({p}_{\text{NH} 3}\right)}^{2} \cdot {p}_{{H}_{2} \text{S}} = {\left(2 \text{p} + 2 \text{q}\right)}^{2} \cdot \text{p} = \text{9.0} \times {10}^{- 3}$

${K}_{\text{p} \text{2}} = {\left({p}_{\text{NH} 3}\right)}^{2} \cdot {p}_{{H}_{2} \text{S} \text{e}} = {\left(2 \text{p} + 2 \text{q}\right)}^{2} \cdot \text{q} = \text{4.5} \times {10}^{- 3}$

$∴ \dfrac{\text{p}}{\text{q}} = 2 ⇒ \text{p} = 2 \text{q}$

$∴ {K}_{\text{p} 1} = {\left(\text{2p} + \text{p}\right)}^{2} \cdot \text{p} = \text{9.0} \times {10}^{- 3}$

$∴ \text{p} = \text{0.1} \text{atm} \text{and} \text{q} = \dfrac{\text{0.1}}{2} = \text{0.05}$

Total pressure = 2p + 2q + p + q = 3p + 3q

= 3 × 0.1 + 3 × 0.05 = 0.45 atm

$\text{2}{\text{AB}}_{2} \text{(g)} ⇌ \text{2}\text{AB(g)} + {B}_{2} \text{(g)}$
The degree of dissociation is $\text{x}$ and is small as compared to $\text{1}$ . The expression relating the degree of dissociation $\text{(x)}$ with equilibrium constant ${K}_{P}$ and total pressure $\text{P}$ is:

At equilibrium \text{2(1} - \text{x)}\text{2x}\text{x}

Partial pressures
{P}_{{\text{AB}}_{2}} $\$text{=}\dfrac{\text{2(1} - \text{x)}}{\text{2}\text{+}\text{x}} \text{p,}{P}_{\text{AB}} \text{=}\left(\dfrac{\text{2x}}{\text{2}\text{+}\text{x}}\right)\text{p,}{P}_{{B}_{2}} \text{=}\left(\dfrac{x}{\text{2+x}}\right)\text{p}$
${K}_{p} = \dfrac{\text{p} {AB}^{2} {pB}_{2}}{( {pAB}_{2} {)}^{2}} = \dfrac{[ ( \dfrac{2 x}{2 + x} ) \text{p} {]}^{2} [ \dfrac{x \text{p}}{2 + x} ]}{[ \dfrac{2 ( 1 - x )}{2 + x} \text{p} {]}^{2}}$

\left($2 + $\text{x}\right) \to$2$ (\text{x} is small)
\left($1 - $\text{x}\right) \to$1$
${K}_{P} = \dfrac{4x^{3} \text{p}}{8} = \dfrac{x^{3} \text{p}}{2}$
\text{x} = $\dfrac{2\text{kp}}{p}3$

questions.q: When N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub> is heated at certain temperature, it dissociates as ${N}_{2} {O}_{5} \left(\text{g}\right) ⇌ {N}_{2} {O}_{3} \left(\text{g}\right) + {O}_{2} \left(\text{g}\right) {; K}_{c} = \text{2.5}$. At the same time N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> also decomposes as : ${N}_{2} {O}_{3} \left(\text{g}\right)⇌ {N}_{2} \text{O} \left(\text{g}\right) + {O}_{2} \left(\text{g}\right).$If initially 4.0 moles of N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub> are taken in 1.0 litre flask and allowed to dissociation, concentration of O<sub>2</sub> at equilibrium is 2.5 M. Equilibrium concentration of N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub> is :

$\begin{cases}{N}_{2} {O}_{5} & ⇌ & {N}_{2} {O}_{3} & + & {O}_{2} \\ 4 - \text{x} & & \text{x} - \text{y} & & \text{x} + \text{y} \\ {N}_{2} {O}_{3} & ⇌ & {N}_{2} \text{O} & + & {O}_{2} \\ \text{x} - \text{y} & & \text{y} & & \text{y} + \text{x}\end{cases}$

$∵ \left[{O}_{2}\right] = \text{x} + \text{y} = \text{2.5}$

and $\text{2.5} = \dfrac{\left(\text{x} + \text{y}\right) \left(\text{x} - \text{y}\right)}{4 - \text{x}}$

for 1st reaction Kc=$\text{2.5} = \dfrac{\left(\text{x} - \text{2.5} + \text{x}\right) \times \text{2.5}}{4 - \text{x}} = \dfrac{\left(2 \text{x} - \text{2.5}\right)}{4 - \text{x}} 2.5$

$4 - \text{x} = 2 \text{x} - \text{2.5}$

$\text{6.5} = 3 \text{x} ∴ \text{x} = \text{2.166}$

\left[{N}_{2} {O}_{5}\right] = 4 - \text{x} = 4 - \text{2.166} = \text{1.834 M}

at the same time N2O3 also decomposes as ${N}_{2} {O}_{3} \left(\text{g}\right)⇌ {N}_{2} \text{O} \left(\text{g}\right) + {O}_{2} \left(\text{g}\right)
In initially 4 mol of N2O5 are taken in 1 L flask and allowed to dissociate, concentration of O2 at equilibrium is 2.5 M, equilibrium concentration of N2O3 will be$
questions.solution:
Solution writing equilibrium concentrations of simultaneous equilibria (V=1 Litre)

$\mathop{{N}_{2} {O}_{5}}_{4 - \text{x}} ⇌ \mathop{{N}_{2} {O}_{3} \left(\text{g}\right)}_{\text{x} - \text{y}} + \mathop{{O}_{2} \left(\text{g}\right)}_{\text{x} + \text{y}} ; {K}_{c} = \text{2.5}$

$\mathop{{N}_{2} {O}_{3}}_{\text{x} - \text{y}} ⇌ \mathop{{N}_{2} \text{O}}_{y} + \mathop{{O}_{2}}_{\text{x} + \text{y}}$

\left[{O}_{2}\right] = \text{x} + \text{y} = \text{2.5}$

${K}_{c} = \text{2.5} = \dfrac{\left[{N}_{2} {O}_{3}\right] \left[{O}_{2}\right]}{\left[{N}_{2} {O}_{5}\right]} = \dfrac{\left(\text{x} - \text{y}\right) \left(\text{x} + \text{y}\right)}{4 - \text{x}}$

as y = 2.5 - x ; Substituting

$\dfrac{( \text{x} - \text{2.5} + \text{x} ) \left(\text{2.5}\right)}{4 - \text{x}} = \text{2.5}$

\left(2 \text{x} - \text{2.5}\right) = 4 - \text{x}$

$∴ 3 \text{x} = \text{6.5}$

$∴ \text{x} = \text{2.17}$

y = 0.33

\left[{N}_{2} {O}_{3}\right] = \text{x} - \text{y} = \text{2.17} - \text{0.33}$

$\text{x} - \text{y} = \text{1.84} = \left[{N}_{2} {O}_{3}\right]

Choice 1.8

$\begin{cases} & 3 {Se}_{2} \left(\text{g}\right) & ⇌ & {Se}_{6} \left(\text{g}\right) \\ \text{At equilibrium} & \text{a} \left(1 - α\right) & & \dfrac{\text{a} α}{3}\end{cases}$

Total moles at equilibrium $= \text{a} \left($1 - $\dfrac{2 α}{3}\right)

\text{a} \left($1 - $\dfrac{2 α}{3}\right) = {n}_{Total} = \dfrac{\text{PV}}{\text{RT}}

$= $\dfrac{\text{1 atm} × \text{2.463} × 1 {0}^{- 3}}{\text{0.0821} × 3 0 0} =$1 {0}^{- 4}$

\text{1.266}$× 1 {0}^{- 4} \left($1 - $\dfrac{2 α}{3}\right) =$1 {0}^{- 4}$

$1 - $\dfrac{2 α}{3} = \dfrac{1}{\text{1.266}} = \text{0.79}

questions.q:
The equilibrium constant $( {K}_{p} )$ for the decomposition of gaseous ${H}_{2}O$

${H}_{2}O\left(g\right) ⇌ {H}_{2}\left(g\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}{O}_{2} ( g )$

is related to degree of dissociation $( \alpha )$ at a total pressure $p$ is given by
questions.solution:
${H}_{2}O\left(g\right) ⇌ {H}_{2}\left(g\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}{O}_{2} ( g ) 100 ( initally ) 1 - \alpha\alpha\dfrac{α}{2} ( atequilibrium )$

Total moles of water at equilibrium = \left(1 - \alpha\right) + \alpha + \dfrac{α}{2} = 1 - \alpha + \alpha + \dfrac{α}{2} = 1 + \dfrac{α}{2}$

Partial pressure of ${H}_{2}O = partialpressure * molefraction = p * \dfrac{noofmolesofwater}{totalnumberofmoles} = p * \left(\begin{array}{ll}\dfrac{1 - \alpha}{1 + \dfrac{α}{2}}\end{array}\right) = p\left(\begin{array}{ll}\dfrac{2 ( 1 - \alpha )}{2 + \alpha}\end{array}\right)$

Partial pressure of ${H}_{2} = partialpressure * molefraction = p * \dfrac{noofmolesofH}{totalnumberofmoles} = \left(\dfrac{α}{1 + \dfrac{α}{2}}\right)

Partial pressure of ${O}_{2} = partialpressure * molefraction = p * $\dfrac{no: ofmolesofoxygen}{totalnumberofmoles} =$p \left(\dfrac{α}{2 + \alpha}\right)$

${K}_{p} = \dfrac{partialpressuresofpdts}{partialpressureofreactants} = \dfrac{{pH}_{2} . {pO}_{2}^{1 / 2}}{{pH}_{2}O} = \dfrac{p\left(\dfrac{α}{1 + \dfrac{α}{2}}\right) * p\left(\dfrac{α}{2 + \alpha}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}}{p * \left(\dfrac{2 - 2\alpha}{2 + \alpha}\right)} = \dfrac{p\left(\dfrac{2\alpha}{2 + \alpha}\right)p\left(\dfrac{α}{2 + \alpha}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}}{p * \left(\dfrac{2 - 2\alpha}{2 + \alpha}\right)} = \dfrac{\alpha * {α}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}p\dfrac{1}{2}}{( 2 + \alpha{)}^{\dfrac{1}{2}} ( 1 - \alpha )} = \dfrac{p^{\dfrac{1}{2}}{α}^{\dfrac{3}{2}}}{( 2 + \alpha) \dfrac{1}{2} ( 1 - \alpha )}$

${K}_{p} = \dfrac{{\alpha}^{3 / 2}p^{1 / 2}}{\left(1 - \alpha\right){\left(2 + \alpha\right)}^{1 / 2}}

$

questions.q: The effect of temperature on the equilibrium constant is expressed as,& \left({T}_{2}$> {T}_{1}\right){logK}_{2} / {logK}_{1} = $\dfrac{- \Delta H}{2 . 303} \left[\dfrac{1}{{T}_{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{T}_{1}}\right].$ \text{ and } For endothermic reactions, false statement is:$
questions.solution:
Given that:

$log\dfrac{K2}{K1} = \dfrac{- \Delta H}{2 . 303} \left[\dfrac{1}{{T}_{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{T}_{1}}\right].

For endothermic reactions,~$∆ H > 0 .$

Now, for~${T}_{2} > {T}_{1}$:

$⇒ log \left(\dfrac{K2}{K1}\right) = \dfrac{- \Delta H}{2 . 303}\left[\dfrac{{T}_{2} - {T}_{1}}{{T}_{1}{T}_{2}}\right]$⇒ log \left(\dfrac{K2}{K1}\right)$> 0 ⇒ log{K}_{2} - log{K}_{1} > 0 ⇒ log{K}_{2} > log{K}_{1} ∴ {K}_{2} > {K}_{1} .$

So,~ \left[\dfrac{1}{T2} - \dfrac{1}{T1}\right]< 0$.~ ~ ~$( ∴ {T}_{2} > {T}_{1} )$

questions.q: The decomposition of ${HNO}_{3}$~represented below attains equilibrium at a given ${P}_{eq}$<sub>.</sub> and $T$. If we start~$4 {HNO}_{3 \left(c \text{g}\right)} ⇌ 4 {NO}_{2 \left(\text{g}\right)} + 2 {H}_{2} \text{O} \left(\text{g}\right) + {O}_{2 \left(\text{g}\right)}$~with pure ${HNO}_{3}$~having initial pressure ${P}_{i}$<sub>,& </sub>& then at equilibrium which among the following is correct?
questions.solution:
$\begin{cases}4{HNO}_{3\left(\text{g}\right)} & ⇌ & 4{NO}_{2\left(\text{g}\right)} & + & 2{H}_{2}\text{O}\left(\text{g}\right) & + & {O}_{2} & \text{;}{Pressure at equilibrium is P}_{eq.} \\ {P}_{i} & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ {P}_{i} - 4\text{P} & 4\text{P} & 2\text{P} & \text{P}\end{cases}$

${P}_{eq.} = {P}_{i} - 4 \text{P} + 4 \text{P} + 2 \text{P} + \text{P}$

$∴ {P}_{i} - 4 \text{P} = {P}_{eq.} - 7 \text{P} = {P}_{eq.} - 7 {Po}_{2} ; P = {Po}_{2}$

${K}_{P} = \dfrac{{\left({P}_{\text{NO} 2}\right)}^{4} {\left({P}_{{H}_{2} \text{O}}\right)}^{2} {Po}_{2}}{{\left({P}_{\text{HNO} 3}\right)}^{4}}$

$= \dfrac{1 0 2 4 {\left({Po}_{2}\right)}^{7}}{{\left({P}_{eq.} - 7 {Po}_{2}\right)}^{4}} = \dfrac{1 0 2 4 {\left({Po}_{2}\right)}^{7}}{{\left({P}_{i} - 4 {Po}_{2}\right)}^{4}}$

and ${K}_P^{∘} = \dfrac{{\left({P}_{\text{NO} 2}\right)}^{4} {\left({P}_{{H}_{2} \text{O}}\right)}^{2} {Po}_{2}}{{\left({P}_{\text{HNO} 3}\right)}^{4}} \times \dfrac{1}{{\left(P^{0}\right)}^{3}}$

$= \dfrac{{\left(4 \text{P}\right)}^{2 1} \times {\left(2 \text{P}\right)}^{2} \times \text{P}}{{\left({P}_{eq.} - 7 {Po}_{2}\right)}^{4}} \times \dfrac{1}{{\left(P^{0}\right)}^{3}}$

$= \dfrac{1 0 2 4 {\left({Po}_{2}\right)}^{7}}{{\left({P}_{eq.} - 7 {Po}_{2}\right)}^{4}} = \dfrac{1}{{\left(P^{0}\right)}^{3}}$
